🧠 Crypto News Brief: Weekend nerves dominated crypto: Bitcoin briefly lost $80K amid liquidations and ETF outflows, while a wave of wallet exploits and breaches kept security in focus ahead of this week's Fed decision. 📉 Bitcoin Briefly Loses $80K as Weekend Selloff Liquidates $547M Bitcoin slipped under $80,000 during a thin-liquidity weekend selloff before clawing back toward $80,600 on Sunday. CoinGlass data showed $546.88M in crypto liquidations over 24 hours, following heavy U.S. spot ETF withdrawals on October 22–23, with traders now bracing for the Fed's October 27–28 decision. Read full story → 🇰🇷 South Korea Moves to Push Its Crypto Tax Back to 2029 South Korea's presidential office has backed another postponement of the planned 22% crypto gains tax, with lawmakers weighing a move from January 2027 to 2029. Officials cited unfinished collection systems, gaps in overseas transaction reporting and concern for younger investors building wealth through crypto. More details → 🛡️ Electrum Confirms Bitcoin Thefts Behind Critical 4.8.3 Patch Electrum's advisory reveals that malicious servers exploited how pre-4.8.3 versions displayed unconfirmed transactions, swapping pending payments so users bumping fees via Replace-by-Fee unknowingly signed transfers to attackers. Developers confirmed real losses and urge every user to upgrade, downloading only from electrum.org. Read more → 🏴☠️ Flash-Loan Governance Hijack Drains $4.85M From X100 An attacker used a roughly $1.94M Aave flash loan to buy X tokens and seize two of the three "Senate" seats in Ethereum project X100's governance, then passed proposals that drained treasury and liquidity. About $4.85M in USDT was extracted and the X token crashed over 96%, exposing governance with no snapshots, holding periods or timelocks. See details → 🔓 Keystone Data Breach Exposes Hardware Wallet Buyers' Addresses Hardware wallet maker Keystone disclosed that an unauthorized party accessed its e-commerce systems and stole customer names, contact details, shipping addresses and purchase records. Devices, recovery phrases and payment data were not affected, but the company warns customers to expect phishing and fake replacement-device scams.
